newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Fugitive Philippine legislator in rape case held.
newsitem.headline: Fugitive Philippine legislator in rape case held.

text.p: A Philippine congressman in hiding for 23 days after being charged with the statutory rape of an 11-year-old girl was arrested on Friday after soldiers found him on an islet west of Manila, officials said.

"I am confused. I don't know what's happening to me," a handcuffed Romeo Jalosjos told reporters after elite presidential guards captured him on the islet 60 kms (37 miles) from Manila, ending one of the country's biggest manhunts.

Jalosjos, 56, had an armed bodyguard but chose not to fight when six helicopters whirled over the house he was found in in Bataan province, Jose Calimlim, chief of the Presidential Security Group (PSG) told reporters.
Calimlim said Jalosjos came out of the house after "we promised him there would be no bloodshed and we would not kill him".
A judge issued an arrest warrant for Jalosjos on December 26 on two counts of statutory rape and 12 counts of acts of lasciviousness.
When police went to his house, Jalosjos had fled, causing a public uproar with newspapers saying this was yet another example of the rich and powerful being immune from the law.

Jalosjos looked stunned when he was presented to reporters. "There's only one victim in this case and that is me," he said, referring to his previous statements that he had been unjustly tried in the media.
Jalosjos has denied allegations by the girl that he had sex with her several times in his Manila apartment last year after paying up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time.

Calimlim said Jalosjos had drawn up an elaborate escape plan involving a helicopter ride, another trip on a light plane and then a boat journey to Malaysia from where he eventually planned to flee to London.
Travel documents with forged names were prepared for the escape, he said.
Last week, the foreign affairs department sought Jakarta's help in tracing Jalosjos after police said they had received a tip that he had fled to Indonesia.
On Thursday, Indonesia's Antara news agency said authorities in North Sulawesi had begun distributing pictures of Jalosjos.
President Fidel Ramos personally ordered his elite guard to hunt down Jalosjos after critics poked fun at the country's judicial system.
"A job well done," Ramos told Calimlim after presidential guards brought Jalosjos to the palace compound to be presented to the media.
Justice Secretary Teofisto Guingona said those who helped Jalosjos evade arrest would be charged with obstruction of justice. He did not identify them.
